headline: Unanimously approved support for mayor's letter urging Senator Bruce Tarr to reject Mass Save cuts.
summary: The commission also discussed a possible solar project on the Blackburn Rotary and a geothermal drilling project at the GHS parking lot, set to begin in spring. The group agreed to wait for the solar developer to finish its research before scheduling more talks. A public information session for the City Council is planned for late October or early November.
decisions: Unanimously approved support for the mayor's letter to Senator Bruce Tarr on Mass Save funding cuts.
Agreed to hold a public information session for the City Council on the Specialized Building Code and Climate Leaders in late October or early November.
Agreed to wait for the solar company to finish its due diligence before scheduling further discussions on the Blackburn Rotary project.
Agreed to share the job of keeping and distributing the minutes, with the role changing hands every three months.
Agreed to hold the next meeting on Thursday, October 21 at 5 PM in the City Hall Annex conference room.

decision_evidence.quote: A motion to support the mayor's letter. The motion was seconded and then unanimously approved.

The group decided to hold a public information session for the City Council regarding the Specialized Building Code and Climate Leaders in late October or early November, after the Housing Compass Plan vote is completed.
The group agreed to wait for the company to complete their due diligence before scheduling further discussions.
It was suggested that the role might change hands every three months. The group agreed.
Commission members agreed to hold the next Clean Energy Commission meeting Thursday, October 21st at 5 PM in the City Hall Annex conference room.
